title: Probing Spatial and Temporal Dynamics of High-Q Dielectric Metasurfaces with Ultrafast Electron Microscopy
content: High-quality factor (high-Q) dielectric nanocavities are promising platforms for manipulating nanoscale light-matter interactions with applications spanning high-sensitivity optical sensing and molecular spectroscopy to quantum light-sources [1]. High-Q nanoantennas support highly localized resonant modes with minimal radiative losses and strong electromagnetic field confinement. Our lab's VINPix (very-large-scale-integrated high-quality factor nanoantenna pixels) structures are a recent example of high-Q dielectric nanoantennas [2] that feature periodic perturbations, allowing the resonators to couple to normally incident free-space radiation. The resultant guided mode resonances (GMR) have tunable radiation lifetimes that depend on the perturbation magnitude. The resonance is spatially confined to wavelength-scale volumes using photonic crystal mirrors engineered with gradually increasing reflection strengths, allowing for the realization of densely arrayed resonators with individual addressability.
